synoptic.summary: High pressure over the southwestern US keeps the area dry: 0% precipitation and thunder in every launch forecast through Thursday. Tuesday a dry shortwave trough grazes the top of the ridge: flow aloft turns to 315°–340°, 13–18 kt about 5,600 ft above the landings in the morning and 7–12 kt at 3,800 ft, and the launch forecasts hold 320°–360° all day — no morning drainage, so Tuesday favors POM North and Cherry (faces 330° and 305°) and POM South sits in the lee. High pressure rebuilds Wednesday and Thursday with very light flow aloft (mostly 2–9 kt below 5,700 ft) and the normal pattern returns: drainage from 120°–160° in the mornings, a switch to 320°–330° around 14:00 Wednesday. Thursday the launch forecasts keep 170°–190° through the afternoon with no switch — a departure from the usual cycle. The pattern changes this weekend (outside these slots).
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Tomorrow, a dry shortwave trough grazing over the top of the ridge will bring a few degrees of cooling and morning cloud cover, though the overall air mass is so dry that no precipitation is expected. This wave could potentially be strong enough to promote mixing out of valley haze along the Wasatch Front, or at least ventilate the boundary layer to erode some of the haze. High pressure will quickly rebuild with warm and dry conditions lasting through at least Friday.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure was 1021.8 mb at 19:54 Monday, 0.8 mb below 24 h earlier (1022.6 mb) and up 1.6 mb from the afternoon low of 1020.2 mb — essentially steady high pressure with the normal daily swing. Light gradient: the local daily wind cycle dominates except where Tuesday's shortwave pushes flow from 315°–340°.

observations.summary: Readings from 19:35–19:50 Monday evening are current (under 30 min old at report time) but describe Monday evening, about 11 hours before the first slot. The valley is near calm: Salt Lake and Provo airports calm, Alpine 349° at 5 kt (gust 8), Spanish Fork 18° at 3 kt, Lehi 152° at 5 kt before its direction dropped out. South Valley Regional's newest reading is 17:35 (about 2.5 h old) with no wind value — treat as near-stale. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations.
